data.exact_reserve_text:
The financial performance for 2023 has been significantly impacted by increased reserves for the syndicates indirect Russia/Ukraine losses and prior year deterioration for the Casualty business group.
The Casualty business group experienced deterioration to the prior year reserves as a result of construction defect claims in Florida and potential claims arising from building cladding issues in the UK.
Due to the continued adverse development that we have seen during the year additional IBNR of GBP 13.2m was booked in the year bringing the overall reserves for this issue to GBP 79.4m.
IBNR of GBP 9.7m has been booked in 2023 to cover this issue.
specific_events: Russian invasion of Ukraine 2022 (including fate of western-leased aircraft in Russia)
Florida construction defect claims (ongoing, impacting 2014-2019 years)
Grenfell Tower fire 2017 / UK cladding issues

prior_year_events.event_name: Russian invasion of Ukraine / western leased aircraft in Russia
prior_year_events.impact_description: Significant uncertainty over coverage and timing led to modelling of multiple scenarios; ultimate gross reserves increased materially (explicitly noted ultimate gross reserves of GBP 264.5m at 31 December 2023 vs GBP 138.3m at 31 December 2022), with the loss reserve split 95% to the 2021 YOA and 5% to the 2022 YOA.
Increased frequency of lawsuits led to additional IBNR of GBP 13.2m being booked in the year, bringing the overall reserves for this issue to GBP 79.4m (aggregate position across years).

prior_year_events.event_name: Grenfell Tower fire / UK cladding issues
prior_year_events.impact_description: Potential claims arising from building cladding issues resulted in IBNR of GBP 9.7m being booked in 2023 to cover this issue (professional indemnity exposures for architects and design-build companies).

named_events.loss_description: Estimated market loss ~US$50bn; current estimated loss to Atrium ~$31.9m gross and $31.8m net of reinsurance.
Outbreak of military activity led to aircraft losses at Khartoum; current loss estimate ~$15.8m gross and $10.6m net of reinsurance recoveries.
Estimated Atrium cost $4.9m gross and $4.5m net of reinsurance.
Estimated cost to Syndicate $7.4m gross and $7.3m net of reinsurance.
Cost to the syndicate $7.3m gross and net of reinsurance.
Part of combined events costing the syndicate a total of $14.0m gross and net of reinsurance (with Hurricane Idalia).
Part of combined events costing the syndicate a total of $14.0m gross and net of reinsurance (with New Zealand events/Cyclone Gabrielle).

data.standardized_narrative: During 2023 the syndicate strengthened reserves materially, driven primarily by significant uncertainty and adverse development relating to Russian/Ukraine aviation exposures (notably western-leased aircraft in Russia) and prior-year deterioration within the Casualty business due to construction defect litigation in Florida and emerging UK cladding-related PI exposures. Inflation and higher claims costs were also considered in setting best estimate reserves. Overall, gross claims outstanding increased materially year-on-year, with the syndicate applying probabilistic scenario modelling for the Russia/Ukraine exposures and booking additional IBNR for casualty and professional indemnity risks.
raw_causal_phrases: increased reserves for the syndicates indirect Russia/Ukraine losses and prior year deterioration for the Casualty business group.

The Casualty business group experienced deterioration to the prior year reserves as a result of construction defect claims in Florida and potential claims arising from building cladding issues in the UK.
Due to the continued adverse development that we have seen during the year additional IBNR of GBP 13.2m was booked in the year bringing the overall reserves for this issue to GBP 79.4m.
IBNR of GBP 9.7m has been booked in 2023 to cover this issue.
This has resulted in ultimate gross reserves of GBP 264.5m (31 December 2022 - GBP 138.3m), GBP 84.5m (31 December 2022 - GBP 39.2m) net of reinsurance.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development (153.241m) was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (gross cumulative ultimate estimates diagonal comparison) on page 36. Some narrative amounts (e.g. overall reserves for specific issues) are presented net of reinsurance in the text; where only net figures were stated in narrative those were not used as the primary PYD figure. The Russia/Ukraine aviation reserve movement is explicitly quantified in the notes (gross reserves moved to GBP 264.5m from GBP 138.3m) and has been used to attribute the major portion of the PYD to Aviation, but the triangle-based aggregate PYD was used as the authoritative total. Reinsurance to Close and other structural transactions were considered; no obvious distortion to the 2014-2021 columns invalidating the triangle calculation was identified.
